## Excursions to Lake Nordenskjöld: choosing a Torres del Paine trip

[Lake Nordenskjöld](/chile/place/lake-nordenskjold/) is one of the scenic stops on driving routes through [Torres del Paine National Park](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). Its turquoise waters and surrounding mountains look different depending on the weather. When choosing an excursion, another factor matters more: **where the lake stop falls within the overall itinerary and what comes before it**.

We include the lake in three full-day excursions. All combine Nordenskjöld with other attractions in the park, but differ in the style of service and the main portion of the route.

## Three ways to visit

**Standard excursion.** [“Torres del Paine: Milodón, Lakes and Salto Grande”](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/torres-del-paine-standard-milodon-full-day/) starts at 07:00 and ends with a return to [Puerto Natales](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) around 18:45. It first covers the Milodón Cave, lakes along the southern route, and the Grey area. After lunch, scenic stops include [Pehoé](/chile/place/lake-pehoe/), [Salto Grande](/chile/place/salto-grande-waterfall/), and Nordenskjöld.

**Private excursion.** [“Private Day with Milodón and the Lakes”](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) also includes the Milodón Cave, [Grey Lake](/chile/place/lake-grey/), Pehoé, the waterfall, and Nordenskjöld. This option is confirmed as private and includes the entrance fee and lunch at a local restaurant; a separate boat excursion is not listed in its description.

**Day with Grey Glacier.** [“Torres del Paine and Grey Glacier: Boat, Lakes and Milodón”](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) begins with a boat trip **to Grey Glacier**, followed by scenic lake stops, including Nordenskjöld. National park admission, the boat excursion to the glacier, and lunch are included.

Importantly, the boat in the third option visits Grey Glacier, **not Lake Nordenskjöld**. At Nordenskjöld, the itinerary includes scenic viewpoints.

## Nordenskjöld's place in the itinerary

On the current routes, Nordenskjöld is visited together with [Salto Grande Waterfall](/chile/place/salto-grande-waterfall/) and Lake Pehoé. Travelers can see different features of the same mountain landscape: a broad lake, rocky ledges, and water flowing between lakes. On a short stop, the panorama is the main experience rather than a long hike.

If you are interested in independent trekking along the lakeshore or toward viewpoints of the Cuernos mountains, this needs to be arranged separately. A lake appearing on an itinerary **does not guarantee any particular walking trail**. More about its geography and viewpoints is available on the [Lake Nordenskjöld page](/chile/place/lake-nordenskjold/).

## What to agree before traveling

Clarify the length of the stops, whether walks are required, the group arrangements, and the services included in your chosen excursion. All three options include a substantial number of natural sights. Wind and cloud cover can change mountain visibility, while access to paths and viewpoints is governed by CONAF rules. In 2026, the park authority published changes to seasonal restrictions, so route conditions and entrance requirements need to be checked for your travel date.

For a day of sightseeing by road, bring a windproof jacket, waterproof outer layer, and shoes suitable for rocky viewpoints.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions to Lake Nordenskjöld

### Is Lake Nordenskjöld included in the standard park tour?

Yes. The lake is one of the scenic stops on the [standard Milodón excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/torres-del-paine-standard-milodon-full-day/), after Pehoé and Salto Grande.

### Is there an option with private service?

Yes. The [private excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) includes Nordenskjöld and other park lakes, as well as lunch and the entrance fee.

### Do these itineraries include a boat trip on Lake Nordenskjöld?

No such service is promised. One option includes a boat excursion, but it goes to **Grey Glacier**.

## Excursions to Lake Pehoé: Patagonian panoramas and Salto Grande

[Lake Pehoé](/chile/place/lake-pehoe/) is one of the most striking scenic stops in [Torres del Paine National Park](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). Visitors come for views of its waters against the Paine massif and nearby [Salto Grande Waterfall](/chile/place/salto-grande-waterfall/). Unlike a multi-day trek, these lake panoramas can be enjoyed on a full-day sightseeing excursion by road.

We include Pehoé in three current excursion programs. All offer a view of the lake; the key difference is **the style of the trip and which stops come beforehand**.

## Comparing itineraries that visit Pehoé

[“Torres del Paine: Milodón, Lakes and Salto Grande”](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/torres-del-paine-standard-milodon-full-day/) is a standard tour departing early from Puerto Natales. After the Milodón Cave, several lakes, and the Grey area, the route reaches a viewpoint over Pehoé. A walk to Salto Grande follows, along with stops at Nordenskjöld and other scenic locations. The approximate schedule is 07:00–18:45; we agree the exact terms and price when preparing the trip.

[“Private Day with Milodón and the Lakes”](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) covers the same main natural attractions but is confirmed as a private experience. Entrance admission and lunch at a local restaurant are included. The Pehoé and Salto Grande stops come after the visit to the Grey Lake area.

[“Torres del Paine and Grey Glacier: Boat, Lakes and Milodón”](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) adds a boat trip to [Grey Glacier](/chile/place/grey-glacier/) at the start of the day. The excursion then continues through the lakes, including Pehoé. Park entrance tickets, lunch, and the boat trip to the glacier are included.

**A boat trip to Grey Glacier does not mean a catamaran crossing on Pehoé.** Crossings of Lake Pehoé exist as a separate means of transport within the park, but they must not be advertised as included in these excursions without confirmation.

## Why see Pehoé and Salto Grande together?

The Pehoé viewpoint offers a wide panorama of water and mountains. At Salto Grande, the focus shifts to moving water and rocky shores. [Lake Nordenskjöld](/chile/place/lake-nordenskjold/) lies nearby and is connected to this waterscape. The sequence of lake, waterfall, and another lake helps visitors understand the park's geography.

These are **scenic stops** on the excursion programs; an extended hike to other viewpoints is not confirmed. If you want to follow a long trail or spend time photographing the landscape in different light, arrange it separately.

## Weather and access

Strong winds are possible in Patagonia even on a sunny day, and clouds can quickly obscure the mountains. Viewpoints near the water can have wet stones and gusts of wind. Bring a warm layer, a windproof jacket, and shoes with good grip.

CONAF publishes current restrictions on trails, entrance tickets, and seasonal park infrastructure. Your travel date therefore affects access to additional walks; a sightseeing tour description should not be taken as permission to undertake any trek in the park.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions to Pehoé

### Can I see Pehoé without a multi-day hike?

Yes. It is included in three Ada Tours day trips by road, including the [standard itinerary](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/torres-del-paine-standard-milodon-full-day/).

### Which option should I choose for Grey Glacier?

The [day with a boat trip to Grey Glacier](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) explicitly includes the boat excursion and subsequent stops at Pehoé. Check the weather and operating conditions for the boat service.

### Is a separate crossing of Lake Pehoé included?

No such crossing is listed in the available descriptions of these three excursions. Viewing the lake should not be confused with taking water transport across it.

## Excursions to Lake Porteño: the approach to Torres del Paine

[Lake Porteño](/chile/place/lake-porteno/) lies on the southern approaches to Torres del Paine National Park in Chilean Patagonia. Excursion itineraries mention it alongside the Milodón Cave, Lake Sofía, and [Lake Toro](/chile/place/lake-toro/). Its role is generally different from that of Pehoé or Grey: **it is a scenic section of a longer driving route**, not a standalone water activity offered as part of the trip.

Our three excursions through the Porteño area include several lakes and nature stops. To choose the right one, compare not only whether Porteño is mentioned but also the rest of the day's itinerary.

## Three routes that include Porteño

The [standard “Milodón, Lakes and Salto Grande” excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/torres-del-paine-standard-milodon-full-day/) departs at approximately **07:00**. After the Milodón Cave and Lake Sofía, it passes through the Porteño area, the Mesa mountains, and Lake Toro. Travelers then visit the [Grey area](/chile/place/lake-grey/), [Pehoé](/chile/place/lake-pehoe/), Salto Grande, and other viewpoints. The return to Puerto Natales is around 18:45.

The [private Milodón and Lakes excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) also mentions Porteño among the landscapes on the approach to the park. This is a private itinerary with admission and lunch included; a boat trip on Porteño is not listed.

The [Grey Glacier day with a boat excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) is built around a boat trip to Grey Glacier followed by an extensive sightseeing route. The latter part includes the Lake Porteño area. Glacier navigation, park admission, and lunch are included; the position of individual stops depends on the day's actual timetable.

## Porteño: roadside views or a walk to the shore?

A lake being named among the places visited **does not by itself confirm a shoreline walk, swimming, or a boat excursion**. Ask where a safe photo stop is possible and how much time it allows. In Patagonia, even a short stop outside the car may require protection from strong winds.

Lake Porteño should not be confused with [Lake Toro](/chile/place/lake-toro/) or with Pehoé, which comes later in the excursion sequence. These lakes form part of one extensive scenic route but have different viewpoints.

## Practical logistics from Puerto Natales

CONAF lists **Road Y-290**, known as the Lago Porteño route, among the approaches to the park from [Puerto Natales](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). This explains why Porteño appears in itineraries before the better-known lakes and waterfalls. A tour of the wider Torres del Paine area takes a long day, and the actual number of stops may vary with the weather and road conditions.

For this excursion, pack several warm layers, a windproof jacket, and comfortable shoes, even if you spend most of the day in a vehicle. The park authorities regulate trail access and current entrance requirements.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions to Lake Porteño

### Is there a separate boat excursion on Porteño?

No such product is confirmed in the current Ada Tours catalog. The lake appears in three Torres del Paine excursions as part of the natural scenery along the route.

### Is Porteño part of the private excursion?

Yes. The [private day with Milodón and the lakes](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) explicitly lists Lake Porteño among its panoramas.

### How does Porteño differ from Pehoé on the itinerary?

Porteño is on the approach to the park's main scenic areas. [Pehoé](/chile/place/lake-pehoe/) is featured together with Salto Grande Waterfall at a later stage of the route.

## An excursion to Lake Sarmiento in Chilean Patagonia

[Lake Sarmiento](/chile/place/lake-sarmiento/) is known for broad views across the water toward the mountains and steppes of Torres del Paine. Its shores and open sky offer a different perspective on Patagonia from the region's gorges, forests, and waterfalls. Depending on cloud cover, the mountain silhouettes may be clearly visible or almost completely hidden.

For travelers, the important distinction is the type of visit: on the Ada Tours excursion, the lake is one of the nature stops on **a full sightseeing day**, not a destination for a dedicated water-based trip.

## Which excursion includes Lake Sarmiento?

The current [“Torres del Paine and Grey Glacier: Boat, Lakes and Milodón” excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) combines several landscapes in one day. The itinerary begins with a boat trip to Grey Glacier, followed by an overland tour of the park and surrounding areas.

The stops include Lake Sofía, the Prat and Mesa mountain ranges, Lake Toro, Pehoé, Salto Grande Waterfall, Lake Nordenskjöld, Laguna Amarga, and **Lake Sarmiento**. The Milodón Cave is also part of the excursion.

The included services are national park entrance tickets, a boat trip **to Grey Glacier**, and lunch. The boat portion is specifically at Grey, not Sarmiento. The published description does not promise a cruise on Lake Sarmiento, a separate excursion to its islands, or a trek all the way around it.

## What a stop at Sarmiento offers

The open shore reveals the combination of water, Patagonian steppe, and mountains. Photographic conditions depend on the sun's position and the wind, so it is useful to allow time for a few different views rather than counting on a single required shot.

The lake is particularly interesting as one link in a long chain of contrasting landscapes. [Grey Lake](/chile/place/lake-grey/) and its namesake glacier offer the experience of glacial water and icebergs; [Lake Toro](/chile/place/lake-toro/) reveals the wide-open southern edges of the park. Sarmiento adds an expansive steppe perspective.

If Sarmiento is the main objective of your trip, agree in advance how long the stop will be. On a full-day excursion, time must be shared among many natural attractions.

## Preparing for a day visiting several lakes

The trip takes place in Patagonia, where strong winds are possible in exposed areas even under sunny skies. A substantial jacket, comfortable shoes, and protection for equipment against rain are useful. Conditions on the boat trip to the glacier may differ from those at overland viewpoints, and whether the boat can operate depends on the weather.

For the detailed sequence, consult the [Grey Glacier excursion page](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/). When choosing travel dates, you can also explore [Chile tours](/chile/tour/), but the presence of a lake's name on another itinerary does not confirm how it will be visited.

## Frequently asked questions about Lake Sarmiento

### Is a boat trip on Lake Sarmiento included?

No. The boat portion of this excursion goes to Grey Glacier. Lake Sarmiento is listed among the overland nature stops.

### Can I visit Sarmiento and Grey Glacier in one day?

Yes. Both are included in the same [Ada Tours excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/). The order and possibility of leaving the vehicle at particular stops depend on the weather and the day's actual plan.

### Is this excursion suitable for travelers primarily interested in nature photography?

Yes. The route includes lakes, mountains, a glacier, and a waterfall. However, visibility of the peaks and the weather cannot be guaranteed in advance.

## Excursions via Lake Sofía: choosing a Torres del Paine itinerary

[Lake Sofía](/chile/place/lake-sofia/) lies near Puerto Natales, on the approach to Chilean Patagonia's scenic routes. Its calm water, surrounding slopes, and open sky make the area a pleasant introduction to the local landscape.

We include Lake Sofía in **three Torres del Paine excursions**. All feature it as part of a longer sightseeing day. None of these itineraries describes a dedicated hike around the lake or kayaking on its waters as an included activity.

## Which excursions pass Lake Sofía?

| Program | Key difference |
|---|---|
| [Private day](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) | Private format and overland stops |
| [Milodón and Salto Grande](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/torres-del-paine-standard-milodon-full-day/) | Detailed sightseeing itinerary, 07:00–18:45 |
| [Grey Glacier by boat](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) | Boat excursion to the glacier plus land-based views |

Compare the format, schedule, and included services for each option. Lake Sofía is one of the stops along the way in all three, so the lake's name alone is not enough to choose between them.

## Private excursion: the Milodón Cave and lakes

The [private Torres del Paine excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) is a full-day experience. It includes the Milodón Cave, views of Lake Sofía, the Prat range, Lakes Porteño and Toro, and then the Grey area, Pehoé, and Salto Grande.

This private excursion includes admission and lunch in a local restaurant. A separate boat excursion to the glacier is not listed among the included services for this option.

## Standard sightseeing day and the glacier route

The [standard excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/torres-del-paine-standard-milodon-full-day/) is scheduled to depart at **07:00** and return to Puerto Natales around **18:45**. After the Milodón Cave, the itinerary covers Lake Sofía and other lakes, mountain views, Salto Grande Waterfall, and park viewpoints.

The [Grey Glacier option](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) additionally confirms a boat trip to the glacier. National park admission and lunch are also included. It is the option to choose if the highlight you want is approaching the glacier front from the water, with Lake Sofía contributing to the broader scenery of the area.

## What is special about Lake Sofía?

The lake lies in a transition zone between more sheltered valleys and open Patagonian landscapes. The combination of water, clouds, and surrounding slopes makes it interesting for photography. It shows how varied the scenery can be within a short distance of Puerto Natales.

A longer lakeshore walk requires a separate arrangement. On a sightseeing excursion, the lake may be a brief stop or a panorama seen from the road; the published itineraries do not specify a particular beach, free walking time, or water activities on Sofía.

If a walking route is your priority, ask in advance which stretch of shore is accessible and how much time is available. Conditions can change even during a single sightseeing day.

## Frequently asked questions about Lake Sofía

### Is Lake Sofía included in every Torres del Paine excursion?

Not necessarily. The Ada Tours catalog lists it in the three specific excursions above. Other itineraries should be checked individually.

### Which excursion includes a boat trip to the glacier?

The [“Grey Glacier: Boat, Lakes and Milodón” itinerary](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/). The boat goes to Grey Glacier, not across Lake Sofía.

### Which option is better for an easy sightseeing day?

Compare the private and standard programs by duration, guiding arrangements, and number of stops. Only the designated private excursion offers private service, which does not by itself mean there are no long transfers or challenging walking sections.

### Do I need warm clothes in summer?

Yes. Wind protection and extra layers are useful in Patagonia even if the day begins with relatively mild weather.
